sections.label: Cleaner energy vehicles by 2040
sections.summary: The vision is for all vehicles in Singapore to run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Our vision is for all vehicles in Singapore to run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sections.label: Island-wide public EV charging network
sections.summary: An island-wide public charging network is needed, with 60,000 charging points aimed for by 2030 and 12,000 more awarded across HDB carparks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To further encourage the EV transition, we need an island-wide public charging network that is safe, reliable and accessible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We aim to deploy 60,000 charging points across Singapore by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: LTA recently awarded a tender to deploy an additional 12,000 charging points across all HDB carparks.

sections.label: Penalties for non-homologated model supply
sections.summary: Supplying a non-homologated model is an offence, with individuals facing a maximum $20,000 fine or 24 months' jail, and corporate entities a maximum $40,000 fine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The supply of a non-homologated model is an offence with the penalty for individuals of a maximum fine of $20,000 or a maximum jail term of 24 months, or both, while a corporate entity faces a maximum fine of $40,000.

sections.label: Licensing of EV charging operators
sections.summary: EV charging operators must obtain a licence valid for three years and renewable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: EV charging operators must obtain a licence, which will be valid for three years and renewable.

sections.label: Developer electrical infrastructure and charging points
sections.summary: Developers must install electrical infrastructure supporting at least 1.3 kilovolt amperes per car and motorcycle lot, and charging points drawing at least one-fifth of that power.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: First, developers must install electrical infrastructure that supports at least 1.3 kilovolt amperes of power for every car and motorcycle parking lot in the development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Second, developers must install a minimum number of charging points which would draw at least one-fifth of that amount of power.

sections.label: Ordinary resolution for EV charger installation
sections.summary: Related amendments to the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act were proposed so installing or uninstalling EV chargers in strata-titled developments requires only an ordinary resolution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This is because under the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act 2004, proposals to lease the common property to EV charging operators to install EV chargers could be required to meet a resolution threshold of up to 90%, depending on the duration of the lease.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Hence, in consultation with MND and BCA, we proposed related amendments to the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act so that proposals to install or uninstall EV chargers in strata-titled developments will only require an ordinary resolution, which can be passed with the support of a simple majority of the subsidiary proprietors voting in a general meeting.

sections.label: Transport carbon emissions share
sections.summary: In 2020, transport accounted for 16% of Singapore's carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As recently as 2020, transport accounted for 16% of Singapore's carbon emissions.

sections.label: EV charger approval, registration, licensing
sections.summary: EV chargers must be LTA-approved and labelled, registered with a responsible person, and charging service providers must be licensed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, EV chargers must be approved by LTA as an approved model and affixed with an approval label before it can be supplied or used in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Second, EV chargers must be registered with LTA and specify a registered responsible person before it can be used to charge any EV in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Third, persons who provide EV charging services in Singapore or engages in conduct as a charging station operator must be licensed.

sections.label: Certification by prescribed persons
sections.summary: Clauses 23 and 24 require certification by a prescribed competent person and a prescribed person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Clauses 23 and 24 of the Bill provide that the certification will have to be done by a prescribed competent person and a prescribed person.

sections.label: Record retention for EV chargers
sections.summary: The Bill requires the registered responsible person for an EV charger to keep records such as certificates for at least two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Bill also requires the registered responsible person for an EV charger to keep and retain records, such as certificates, going back at least two years.

sections.label: Notice of safety-related defects
sections.summary: Clause 35 requires a manufacturer or supplier aware of a safety-related defect to notify registered responsible persons for chargers of the same model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Second, clause 35 requires a manufacturer or supplier of an EV charger who becomes aware of any safety-related defect in the EV charger to give notice to every registered responsible person for a registered-for-charging EV charger of the same model, among others.

sections.label: Question on regulating charging costs
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Bill and subsidiary legislation would regulate commercial aspects such as charging cost ceilings or cost-increase mechanisms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One, would this Bill and its subsidiary legislation, if passed, regulate the commercial aspects of how EVCOs conduct their business, for example, by imposing ceilings on charging costs or mechanisms to regulate any increase in charging costs?

sections.label: LTA step-in and EVCO sector
sections.summary: The speaker says LTA's step-in power is useful but a vibrant EVCO sector matters more, and asks about LTA's long-term plans and future omnibus legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Two, LTA's power to order a step-in arrangement under Part 7 of the Bill is a useful power, but LTA's role in encouraging a vibrant and competitive EVCO sector is equally, if not more, important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Where an EVCO has its licence suspended, revoked or surrendered, instead of externalising the costs to taxpayers by ordering a step-in, a vibrant and competitive EVCO sector would mean that market forces can be counted on to secure a replacement EVCO for continuity of services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Having regard to the large tenders which have already gone out this year, what are LTA's optimal long-term plans in terms of the number of EV charging points, percentage of HDB carparks that are EV charging lots and so on?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Three, are there any plans to develop this legislation in future to go beyond regulating the EV chargers and become an omnibus Act that will cover all aspects of our EV transition?

sections.label: Parts 2 to 7 standards
sections.summary: Parts 2 through 7 of the Bill empower LTA to constrain unregulated or inadequately maintained chargers by imposing minimal standards.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Parts 2 through 7 of the Bill empower LTA to constrain unregulated or inadequately maintained chargers by imposing minimal standards.

sections.label: Part 8 charging network
sections.summary: Part 8 requires new buildings with car parks to install charging points for around 4% of total car and motorcycle lots.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Part 8 will expand the charging network by requiring new buildings with car parks to install charging points for – as Minister Iswaran helpfully clarified, the technical mumbo jumbo – around 4% of the total car and motorcycle lots.

sections.label: ECCG and hurdle rate
sections.summary: LTA launched the Electric Vehicle Common Charger Grant in July last year, and the Bill relaxes the hurdle rate for charger installation and removal to a simple majority.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In July last year, LTA launched the Electric Vehicle Common Charger Grant (ECCG) to promote the installation of charging infrastructure in non-landed private residences, a practice in line with other nations, such as Canada and the United Kingdom.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This Bill further relaxes the hurdle rate for the installation and removal of chargers, along with other charger management functions, to a simple majority.

sections.label: Backloaded EV registration strategy
sections.summary: The speaker describes a backloaded strategy permitting only EV registrations after 2030, or a gradualist strategy with EV-specific COE permits and temporary incentives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The first is to adopt a fairly aggressive but backloaded strategy consistent with the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This means only permitting the registration of EVs after that year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The advantage of this approach is that it allows the existing electric charging infrastructure to roll out over the course of the next seven years without too much excess pressure from latent demand.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We can pursue a more gradualist strategy where we begin the issuance of EV-specific COE permits next year, with an even split between the permits available for EVs and ICE vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To further promote EV adoption, we could even provide temporary incentives that would favour the switch to EVs, such as a 10% discount, for instance, on the COE's face value for EV permits.

sections.label: Full EV fleet by 2042
sections.summary: Done incrementally over 20 years, the full EV fleet target would be met by 2042, two years after the 2040 deadline.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Done this way, incrementally, over 20 years, we would meet our full EV fleet target by 2042, only two years after the 2040 deadline, with a more gradual process that simultaneously begins with the EV transition occurring earlier.

sections.label: EV operating cost report
sections.summary: A 2022 paultan.org report said EVs were 8.4% of new Singapore car registrations and operating costs were up to 82% greater.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think he used the number of 80%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: This was based off a report in 2022, reported in paultan.org that said "EVs made up just 8.4% of new cars registered in Singapore with Grab drivers being reluctant to switch".

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And it says 80% higher operating costs for EVs?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: That the estimated operating costs for EVs was as much as 82% greater, yes, based on that report.

sections.label: EV charging point expansion
sections.summary: The EV Charging Bill and an LTA tender for 12,000 charging points in 2,000 HDB car parks will transform Singapore's charging network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the EV Charging Bill that mandates private buildings to provide charging points and the recent LTA tender to install 12,000 EV charging points across 2,000 HDB car parks, Singapore will be transformed from a city with few charging points to a country with probably the highest number of charging points per capita.

sections.label: Norwegian EV buyer survey
sections.summary: A Norwegian Electric Vehicle Association survey found 26% of Norwegian car buyers chose EVs for environmental reasons and 72% for financial reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Yet, only 26% of the car buyers in Norway buy EVs because they are environmentally conscious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, about 72% of the car buyers confessed that they buy EVs because of financial considerations, according to the survey conducted by the Norwegian Electric Vehicle Association.

sections.label: HDB charging points and range anxiety
sections.summary: Installing EV charging points in HDB car parks under the plan for 60,000 points by 2030 will reduce range anxiety and add charging convenience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: But the reason why PHC drivers and the taxi drivers are reluctant to switch to an EV is because of the charging facilities right now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to say that the installation of EV charging points in HDB car parks as part of the Government's plan to deploy 60,000 charging points by 2030 will reduce the range anxiety and provide the convenience of charging EVs.

sections.label: HDB EV charging rates
sections.summary: Under new HDB EV charging contracts awarded by LTA, different operators will charge different rates at different car parks due to differing concession fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Under the new HDB EV charging contracts awarded by LTA, I understand different operators will have different EV charging rates at different HDB car parks due to the different concession fees that they will pay to LTA.

sections.label: Number of LEWs
sections.summary: As of end June 2022, there were 4,000 licensed electrical workers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: As of end June 2022, we know there were 4,000 LEWs in Singapore.

sections.label: Global EV buyer survey
sections.summary: A global survey found 52% of consumers look to buy EVs, a 22% rise in two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: According to a global survey, the number of consumers looking to buy EVs globally has hit 52% and it represents a 22% rise in just two years.

sections.label: China EV fires
sections.summary: In China there were 680 EV fires in the first quarter of this year alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In China, apparently, there were 680 EV fires in the first quarter of this year alone.

sections.label: EV cost and ICE phase-out
sections.summary: A quote says EV ownership costs 82% more than ICE, and the Green Plan stops ICE COE permits after 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The specific quote is that "the total cost of owning an electric vehicle remains 82% higher than owning an equivalent internal combustion engine." So, that is the first clarification.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The second clarification is that my understanding of the Government's position is that the Green Plan states that they will stop issuing ICE COE permits after 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Based on that assumption, my guess is that the complete phase-out of the ICE fleet would occur around 2040, I believe.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: My alternative suggestion would have pushed it back by just two years, but it would actually get a small number, an increasing number of EVs on the road in the interim.

sections.label: Charging points by 2030
sections.summary: The longer-term goal was 60,000 charging points island-wide by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The longer-term goal was to have 60,000 charging points island-wide by 2030.

sections.label: EVs registered end 2021
sections.summary: As of end 2021, about 3,700 electric vehicles were registered, double the previous year's numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: As of end 2021, we had approximately 3,700 electric vehicles registered on the road, double the previous year's numbers.

sections.label: Chargers needed by 2025
sections.summary: Calculations determined that 12,000 chargers might be necessary by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Evidently, some calculations have gone into determining that 12,000 chargers might be necessary by 2025.

sections.label: Charger count and EV adoption
sections.summary: Twelve thousand chargers island-wide may not be enough if EV adoption is successfully encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Twelve thousand chargers island-wide may not be enough if we are successful in encouraging EV adoption.

sections.label: Electrifying heavy vehicle fleets
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOT would consider legislating fleet electrification by a set date and funding fast-charging points and EV research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While an electric heavy vehicle range might understandably be shorter, say approximately 200-kilometre range on a single charge, Government support would be a powerful incentive to modernise and "green" a domestic transport fleet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: As a topic for discussion or consideration, would MOT even consider a more prescriptive approach, say, legislating a requirement for a fleet to be completely electrified by a set date and support fleet owners by dedicating public resources to building large-scale fast-charging points at central areas, such as the port and strategically-placed distribution hubs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Similar to the point made for charging infrastructure for private vehicles, Government funding for charging infrastructure will give industry stakeholders the assurance that the large-scale investment will not bankrupt their company or have too large an impact on their bottom line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Specifically, she mentioned how R&D for NEWater and desalination increased Singapore's profile as a leading global HydroHub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I hope that our Government has also been actively looking for similar R&D opportunities in areas relating to EVs and EV charging (EVC) technology, including charging facility, charging infrastructure or even battery technology.

sections.label: Adoption rate new high
sections.summary: The adoption rate reached a new high of nearly 20% in the past couple of months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In fact, this adoption rate has reached a new high of nearly 20% in the past couple of months.

sections.label: Charging points and charger regulation
sections.summary: By 2030 there will be over 60,000 EV charging points, and LTA should regulate EV chargers given global charging fire risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: By 2030, there will be over 60,000 EV charging points, of which 40,000 will be located in public car parks, whilst 20,000 will be in private premises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Globally, nearly 25% of EV fires occur while charging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: As such, it is vital that we can minimise the deployment of unregulated or ill-maintained chargers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: I agree that LTA should have the power to regulate the supply, modification, advertisement, installation, certification, registration, use and maintenance of EV chargers.

sections.label: Taxi and private hire EV uptake
sections.summary: Driving EV uptake among private hire and taxi drivers is imperative, and full taxi and private hire EVs are under 5% of the fleet.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What this means for the EV ecosystem in Singapore is that it is just as imperative to drive the uptake of EVs among private hire and taxi drivers as it is for other vehicles in order for the Bill to realise its long-term goals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I understand that full taxi and private hire EVs on the road are now less than 5% of Singapore's fleet size and we do have some miles to go before we sleep in this critical pivot.

sections.label: Charging needs of P2P drivers
sections.summary: Charging is a more pressing need for point-to-point drivers, who may travel over 300 kilometres a day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On distance, given that some taxi and private hire drivers easily travel over 300 kilometres a day – multiple times the distance travelled by the average driver – charging becomes a much more pressing need for our point-to-point (P2P) drivers.

sections.label: Charging costs for drivers
sections.summary: A speaker calls on the Government to waive parking costs for private hire and taxi drivers charging their EVs in CBD car parks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Should a private hire or taxi driver need to charge their vehicle, say, after a job in the CBD, a stopover at a charging station in the CBD could set them back at least $2 to $3 an hour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we figure out how to incentivise early adopters to make the transition to EVs, the last thing we want to do is to disincentivise them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, I call on the Government to ease the transition of private hire and taxi drivers to EVs by perhaps waiving the costs of parking in such car parks for them as they are charging their vehicles.

sections.label: Driver's charging break routine
sections.summary: A driver now drives four to five hours at a time, stopping to charge and take a 45-minute break each time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Instead of driving for hours on end, running a full tank of petrol to zero, he now drives for four to five hours at a time, stopping to charge his vehicle, and taking a well-needed 45-minute break each time.

sections.label: Inclusive EV rollout vision
sections.summary: The Bill envisions seamless EV use, and the P2P driving community backs it while urging an inclusive rollout considering diverse driver needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Bill paints a vision of a future where the usage of EVs is seamless and ubiquitous – a smarter, more sustainable future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our P2P driving community and I stand behind this move.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, as a society in transition, we highlight the importance of an inclusive and considered rollout and implementation that take into account a diversity of needs because of the varying types of drivers out there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While the dust settles on the plan, the unions and our associations will continue to work the ground and engage with our major stakeholders to give our inputs to the implementation plan.

sections.label: Charging network and ZEV goal
sections.summary: The Government plans 2,000 public housing car parks with EV chargers by 2025 and 60,000 chargers by 2030, and Singapore joined the ZEV Deployment Goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To support this growth, the Government has already set to boost Singapore's charging network – 2,000 public housing car parks equipped with EV chargers by 2025 and a network of 60,000 chargers by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Just last week, on 18 November, Singapore had accepted the United States' invitation to join the Collective 2030 Zero-Emission Vehicle (ZEV) Deployment Goal (Goal) which represents a shared aspiration among like-minded countries in transiting to a greener land transport sector, at the 2022 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP27).

sections.label: Hybrid vehicles reaching deregistration
sections.summary: The Bill does not address car battery recycling, but many hybrid vehicles like the Honda Vezel and Toyota Vios will soon reach their 10th year and be scrapped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Though this Bill does not talk about recycling of car batteries, we will start to see many of our hybrid vehicles like the Honda Vezel, Toyota Vios reaching their 10th year and will be deregistered and sent for scrap soon.

sections.label: Charging network commitment
sections.summary: The Government has committed to a charging network with around 2,000 housing estate parking spaces equipped with EV chargers by 2025 and around 60,000 chargers by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Malay):  : To support the growth of electric vehicles or EVs in the coming years, the Government has committed to develop a charging network in Singapore, with around 2,000 parking spaces in housing estates to be equipped with EV chargers by 2025, and around 60,000 chargers by 2030.

sections.label: Recycling lithium-ion car batteries
sections.summary: The passage asks how lithium-ion batteries in hybrid and electric cars can be recycled and whether legislation is being reviewed for efficient, sustainable recycling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How can we recycle lithium-ion batteries in hybrid/electric cars?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Is the Government reviewing legislation to ensure that hybrid and electric vehicles can be recycled efficiently and sustainably?

sections.label: Electric car labour needs
sections.summary: According to CNN in 2019, building an electric car requires about 30% less labour than a traditional ICE vehicle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to CNN in 2019, building an electric car requires about 30% less labour than a traditional ICE vehicle.

sections.label: EV charging points and licensing
sections.summary: By 2025 every multi-storey car park will have at least three EV charging points, and the proposed licensing regime raises three challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By 2025, every multi-storey car park will have at least three EV charging points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The proposed licensing regime raises three challenges: first, higher compliance costs; second, the tedious entry into market may prevent smaller businesses from attempting this shift and, hence, limiting market competition; and third, the licensing and certification costs may, subsequently, be passed on to consumers.

sections.label: Two persons inspecting chargers
sections.summary: The proposed framework would require two competent persons, an LEW and a charger equipment specialist, to inspect charger safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The proposed framework would require in future two competent persons, an LEW and a charger equipment specialist, with different expertise, to inspect the safety of the charger.

sections.label: CPFTA controlled goods provisions
sections.summary: Under the CPFTA, clause 5 provides for registering a controlled goods supplier and clause 6 for adding items to the controlled goods list.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Under the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act, or CPFTA, Part 2, clause 5, there is a provision for registering a controlled goods supplier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In clause 6, there is also a provision to add items into the controlled goods list.

sections.label: Idling charge enforcement authority
sections.summary: The passage says market-based solutions like idling charges may not solve the issue and seeks by-law updates giving Town Councils and MCSTs greater penalty authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Market-based solutions, such as imposing an idling charge, may not solve the issue as EVCOs, technically, achieve better unit economies for imposing idling charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I seek the Ministry to study this potential issue and update the by laws that provide Town Councils and MCSTs greater authority to enforce penalties on idling.

sections.label: EV common charger grant
sections.summary: LTA provides the EV common charger grant to support condominiums in installing EV chargers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: LTA provides the EV common charger grant to support condominiums in installing EV chargers.

sections.label: Petrol vehicle phase-out plan
sections.summary: Singapore plans to phase out petrol vehicles and only allow registration of EVs from 2030 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore plans to phase out petrol vehicles and only allow registration of EVs from 2030 onwards.

sections.label: Charging point adequacy concerns
sections.summary: Residents are concerned about charging point adequacy, with a target of 60,000 EV charging points by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the meantime, many of my residents are already concerned about the adequacy of charging points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I note that we have a target of 60,000 EV charging points by 2030.

sections.label: MCST voting threshold reduced
sections.summary: LTA reduced the percentage of votes required at a general meeting for MCSTs of strata-titled developments to pass EV-related resolutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This may present a missed opportunity towards the adoption of EV vehicles due to the reluctance of building owners to create more charging infrastructure due to current prohibitive costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am glad LTA has reduced the percentage of votes required at a general meeting for MCSTs of strata-titled developments to pass EV-related resolutions.

sections.label: Brownfield EV charging challenges
sections.summary: Building a new EV charging station on brownfield sites presents challenges and additional requirements, with about 22 EV charging operators as of July 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Building a new EV charging station on brownfield sites presents many challenges and these are additional requirements imposed on them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There are about 22 EV charging operators as of July 2022.

sections.label: Small-scale provider exit concern
sections.summary: Consumers worry a small-scale provider may secure charging rights at their residence then exit prematurely, raising whether SP would step in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: From the point of view of EV consumers, there is the concern that a small-scale provider secures the right to provide charging points at their residence, then exits the market prematurely when the business becomes unsustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will it be like our energy market, where SP steps in to replace a provider that has exited the market?

sections.label: EV adoption and infrastructure
sections.summary: EV adoption is important for meeting sustainability commitments, and EV success requires infrastructure to be laid out right.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The adoption of EVs is important for us to meet our sustainability commitments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For EVs to be successful, the infrastructure must be laid out right.

sections.label: Transitional arrangements for EV chargers
sections.summary: The Government allows existing suppliers to continue supplying non-approved EV chargers for six months from the Bill's commencement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As part of the transitional arrangements, the Government is allowing existing suppliers to continue to supply non-approved EV chargers for six months from the commencement of the Bill.

sections.label: EV Early Adoption Incentive
sections.summary: MOT launched the EEAI from January 2021 to December 2023, giving fully electric car owners a 45% ARF rebate capped at $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: MOT had also launched an EV Early Adoption Incentive (EEAI) which runs from January 2021 to December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under this scheme, owners who register fully electric cars receive a rebate of 45% off the Additional Registration Fees (ARF), capped at $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As 2022 to mid-2025 is the period with the lowest COE quotas in a 10-year cycle, not many owners will be keen to switch to EVs earlier as their COEs are due later, after 2025.

sections.label: MCST EV charging motion threshold
sections.summary: The amendment lets MCSTs install and regulate EV charging with a motion passed by more than 50% of votes, down from 90%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendment allows MCSTs to install and regulate EV charging by passing a motion with more than 50% of the votes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This would be a sharp drop from the current threshold of 90%.

sections.label: Approved electrical load and charging points
sections.summary: The standard for approved electrical load rose from 15% to 20% of parking lots, and charging points from 1% to 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The standard for approved electrical load increased from 15% of parking lots to 20%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The standard for the number of charging points increased from 1% of parking lots to 4%.

sections.label: Approval regime for EV chargers
sections.summary: The approval regime ensures that only safe EV chargers are sold.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The approval regime ensures that only safe EV chargers are sold.

sections.label: Technical Reference 25 underpins regimes
sections.summary: The regimes will be underpinned by Technical Reference 25 (TR25).

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The regimes will be underpinned by Technical Reference 25 (TR25).

sections.label: Fire Code updated for EV chargers
sections.summary: LTA worked with SCDF to update the Fire Code last year to enhance fire safety requirements for buildings installing EV chargers.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: LTA worked with the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) to update the Fire Code last year to enhance the fire safety requirements for buildings that install EV chargers.

sections.label: Action despite dynamic situation
sections.summary: Action cannot wait for everything to stabilise because the situation is dynamic and calls for a response, so focus is on the 12,000 charging-point deployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But we cannot wait for everything to stabilise before taking action because it is a dynamic situation, it is a situation that calls for a response.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is why we have focused on this 12,000 charging-point deployment.

sections.label: Accommodated within current electrical capacity
sections.summary: In most cases, this can be accommodated within the current electrical capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In most cases, this can be accommodated within the current electrical capacity.

sections.label: Low-powered network complemented by high-powered points
sections.summary: The low-powered charging network will be complemented with a smaller number of high-powered charging points across the island.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Our low-powered charging network will be complemented with a smaller number of high-powered charging points across the island.

sections.label: Multi-agency committee established
sections.summary: A multi-agency committee was established, chaired by Senior Minister of State Amy Khor with deputy chair Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Many other questions will arise, some of which have been, in fact, expressed in the course of this debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is why we have established a multi-agency committee, which is chaired by Senior Minister of State Amy Khor and the deputy chair is Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng.

sections.label: EV mandate thresholds for developments
sections.summary: The EV mandate will not apply if existing developments do not cross specified building or electrical work thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As EV adoption is still at an early stage and not evenly distributed across developments, the mandate will not apply if existing developments do not cross the specified building or electrical work thresholds for now.

sections.label: Co-funding EV charger installations
sections.summary: More than 200 chargers were co-funded at over 80 condominiums, with 30 applications pending review.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And as there is greater demand from higher EV adoption, these will form a key impetus, I think, for all developers and owners of developments to further install EV charging infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So far, we have co-funded the installation of more than 200 chargers at more than 80 condominiums, with 30 applications pending review.

sections.label: Charger supply and use rules
sections.summary: After a six-month transitional period, non-homologated chargers cannot be supplied and unregistered chargers cannot be used.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: After the transitional period of six months after the Act commences, chargers that do not belong to a homologated model cannot be supplied, while unregistered chargers cannot be used.

sections.label: HDB car park tender operators
sections.summary: LTA's large-scale tender for HDB car parks was awarded to five operators across 10 areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: LTA's large-scale tender for HDB car parks was awarded to five operators across 10 areas and allows for further injection of competition through future tenders at these car parks.

sections.label: Licensed electrical workers sufficiency
sections.summary: A joint LTA and EMA study found licensed electrical workers sufficient for EV transition demand over 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Based on a joint study by LTA and EMA last year, the number of licensed electrical workers, or LEWs, is expected to be sufficient to meet the increased demand from the EV transition over the next 15 years.

sections.label: National EV Specialist Safety certification
sections.summary: LTA launched the National EV Specialist Safety certification in partnership with SkillsFuture Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In September this year, LTA launched the National EV Specialist Safety (NESS) certification, in partnership with SkillsFuture Singapore.

sections.label: Extended Producer Responsibility e-waste scheme
sections.summary: NEA has implemented an Extended Producer Responsibility scheme since July last year for proper treatment and recycling of electric waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To this end, since July last year, NEA has brought into effect an Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) scheme to ensure the proper treatment and recycling of electric waste.

sections.label: EV adoption incentives and rebates
sections.summary: The EV Early Adoption Incentive and enhanced Vehicular Emissions Scheme provide a combined rebate of up to $45,000 off an electric car's upfront cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In this case, we have incentivised the adoption of EVs through the EV Early Adoption Incentive, or EEAI, and the enhanced Vehicular Emissions Scheme, which, together, provide a combined rebate of up to $45,000 off the upfront cost of an electric car.

sections.label: Commercial Vehicles Emissions Scheme rebates
sections.summary: The Commercial Vehicles Emissions Scheme provides up to $30,000 in rebates for electric light goods vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Commercial Vehicles Emissions Scheme also provides up to $30,000 in rebates for electric light goods vehicles.

sections.label: Electric bus fleet target
sections.summary: About 3,000 of 6,000 buses will be electric by the end of the decade, with the other half likely hybrid.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, it is working and it is working well.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I have already shared that for buses, for example, because LTA is largely the procurer of buses, we will have 50% of our bus fleet, which means about 3,000 out of the 6,000 buses or so will be electric by the end of the decade, and the other half will likely be hybrid.

sections.label: Review of EEAI continuation
sections.summary: The EEAI's continuation beyond next year is being reviewed, taking into account upfront cost gap and life cycle cost differential between ICE vehicles and EVs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Mr Don Wee asked if the EEAI will continue beyond next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We are reviewing this, taking into account the upfront cost gap and life cycle cost differential between an ICE vehicle and an EV.

sections.label: Electric Vehicles Charging Bill
sections.summary: The Electric Vehicles Charging Bill represents a first but major step in the journey to get there.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Electric Vehicles Charging Bill represents a first but major step in our journey to get there.

sections.label: Phasing out ICE vehicles
sections.summary: From 2030, Singapore will move towards cleaner energy vehicles, phasing out ICE so all cars are electric, hybrid or other cleaner sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: What we have said is that, from 2030, we will want Singapore to move towards cleaner energy vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, we will phase out ICE in the flow.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And, therefore, all cars will have to be either electric or you would have hybrids or you may have other new cleaner energy vehicle sources.

sections.label: Market segmentation and supply
sections.summary: More market segmentation reduces supply to each category, inevitably causing at least volatility and potentially higher prices, especially with strong demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Because when you create more segmentation in the market, reduce the supply to each category, the inevitable consequence must be at least volatility and, potentially – and certainly in the kind of environment we are in where demand is strong – higher prices.
